main_text.l: tutc afsidente tantùm & communicata fuisse Christum & potentem factis, & sanctùm moribus. Quae haeresis postea Samosatenū genuit, & futurae Arianorum haereseos fundamenta nō centissima collocabat, & eius praesertim, quae hodie sentit non aliter Deum esse in homine Christo quam in Paulo & Petro. Itaque hanc de Christo fuisse Carpocratianorum sententiā docet Epiphanius his verbis, Εἶναι δ' αὐτὸν ὅμοιον[?] τοῖς ἀνθρώποις, βίῳ δὲ [illegible, ~10 letters] σωφροσύνῃ τε καὶ ἀρετῇ καὶ βίῳ δικαιοσύνης.

4 Christum ad modum caeterorum hominum ex Iosephi patris & Mariae matris femine natum, cuius sola anima in caelū ascenderit, & ibi est, non etiam corpus, quia illius anima robustior & valentior corpore fuit.

5 Carnis resurrectionem negat futuram, Με-τεμψύχωσιν[?] tamen animarum in alia corpora retinet, & probat ex Pythagoreorum & Platonicorum dogmatis, dissimillima tamen ab illis ratione. Nam Plato ad criminum in hac vita perpetratorum iustam ultionem fieri putat, ut animae ex improborum corporibus migrates, post mortem in belluarum corpora, vel hominum seniorum mittantur ad prius scelus eluendum. Carpocrates autem contrà sentit, idcirco post vitam hanc mitti in alia corpora animas hominum, quòd non se satis voluptatibus expleverint & conspurcarint. Unde quae animae temperantius hic vixerint, sæpius in corpora detrudi.
6 Mundum hunc negat à Deo factum, sed ab inferioribus angelis, inter quos praecipuus fit diabolus. Hi sunt nimirum Platonicae philosophiae fructus, & contemptae simplicis & cæle-

page.notes: Greek in the first paragraph is only partly legible: the opening word of the first line and the middle word of the second line are doubtful, and the middle word is marked illegible. The Greek word "Μετεμψύχωσιν" is split across the line end at "Με-" with a printed hyphen; its reading is doubtful. Long s is normalised to s throughout. Printed "fit" in "praecipuus fit" may be "sit". The word "migrates" is as printed. The paragraph ending "cæle-" continues on the following page. Signature "c.iiij." is at the foot.
